Action: Set aside 15 minutes today to study one passage of Scripture deeply. Meditate on it and apply it to your life.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your Word. Help me to study it diligently and rightly divide the truth.

Say this: I study to show myself approved unto God. I rightly divide the word of truth. The Word does not depart from my mouth. I meditate on it day and night. My way is prosperous, and I have good success. I am a student of the Word.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:17 KJV - "Pray without ceasing."
devotionals.devotional:
The call to pray is a timeless call for all believers, especially Christian workers in all generations. One who desires to be spiritually mature must not overlook the place of prayer. Prayer is not only designed for you to receive things from God; it is designed for your spiritual maturity. The greatest need in the work of God today is not just popularity or money; the greatest need is prayer.

Every Christian worker needs a good prayer life. When prayers are adequately employed, you will always have better results. Prayer is one of the greatest resources of the church here on earth. Scripture says, "Pray without ceasing" (*1 Thessalonians 5:17* KJV), and "Men ought always to pray, and not to faint" (*Luke 18:1* KJV).

Through prayers, you encounter the supernatural, which changes and empowers you into spiritual maturity in life and Christian services. Men and women of God who have ever achieved something in Christendom were people who prayed. The child of God moves forward in life when he learns and disciplines himself to kneel before God in prayers. Rise and pray!

Lesson: Prayer is essential for spiritual maturity and effective ministry; you must pray without ceasing.

Action: Set a specific time today to pray. Use a prayer list and be committed to a quiet time with God.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the privilege of prayer. Help me to pray without ceasing and grow in my prayer life.

Say this: I pray without ceasing. I am committed to a good prayer life. Prayer is my greatest resource. I encounter the supernatural through prayer. I am empowered into spiritual maturity. I rise and pray.

devotionals.memoryVerse: John 4:24 KJV - "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth."
devotionals.devotional:
The ever-present God is your object of worship. Any one who has interest in spiritual maturity must discipline himself to worship the living God. A spiritually mature Christian worker will always have strong regards for the presence of God. He does not treat the presence of God with contempt in any way or anywhere. He holds the presence of God in awe and gives God the deep respect that He deserves.

In worship, the spiritually mature Christian glorifies, honours, and extols the ever-living and ever-present God. Scripture says, "God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth" (*John 4:24* KJV). Worship is essential for spiritual maturity and growth. When you worship, you give the Lord the centre stage of your life and yield your whole being to His supremacy and Lordship.

Praise is one of the ways the spiritually mature Christian worker says thank you to God for who He is, what He has done, what He is doing, and what He will do. Scripture says, "Praise ye the Lord: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely" (*Psalm 147:1* KJV). Find reasons to praise God in all situations. It will elevate your heart from daily distractions to lasting confidence in the living God.

Lesson: Worship and praise are essential for spiritual maturity; you must worship God in spirit and truth.

Action: Take time today to worship God intentionally. Sing praises to Him and ascribe worthiness to His name.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can worship You in spirit and truth. Help me to glorify You with my whole being.

Say this: I worship God in spirit and truth. I hold His presence in awe. I glorify, honour, and extol the living God. I praise Him in good and difficult times. Praise is comely for me. I find reasons to praise God daily.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Christian Doctrine
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 7:17 KJV - "If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself."
devotionals.devotional:
Christian doctrine has been defined as the fundamental truths of the Bible faith. It is the teaching or instructions of the Lord that Christian believers must follow and obey as you journey from time to eternity. Although many have tried to avoid the study of Christian doctrine, saying it is dry and boring, neglecting it will make you vulnerable to the devil and false doctrines of false teachers.

It takes knowledge of Christian doctrine to do the will of God. Jesus made this clear when He said, "My doctrine is not mine, but His that sent me. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself" (*John 7:16-17* KJV). All who want to know the will of God and do it rightly must know the Christian doctrine.

The acid test of all the challenges you are having in these last days is true knowledge of Christian doctrine. Many have had shipwreck of their faith for lack of understanding and knowledge of Christian doctrine. If you must do God's will and not derail, you must have a clear knowledge of Christian doctrine. Christian doctrine is your identity and road map for Christian mission.

Lesson: You must know Christian doctrine to do God's will and avoid being deceived by false teachers.

Action: Pick one core doctrine today (e.g., salvation, the Holy Spirit, the church) and study it in the Word.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the truth of Christian doctrine. Help me to know and apply Your doctrine correctly.

Say this: I know Christian doctrine. I am not deceived by false teachers. I do the will of God because I know His truth. My doctrine is from God, not from men. I am grounded in the faith.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And The Harvest
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 4:35 KJV - "Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest."
devotionals.devotional:
The heart of Christ is always on planting the seed of the gospel and harvesting the souls of mankind for God. The Lord says, "Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest" (*John 4:35* KJV).

One of the reasons why you often fail to do the work and will of God is that you never love to look up to the harvest field. You are often looking away from it. You must remember that for the purpose of soul harvest you are called. You can begin to be actively involved in soul harvest by being compassionate toward sinners, sharing the hope of eternal life, healing the broken hearted, setting the captives free, and encouraging the weak in faith.

Jesus saw the multitudes and was moved with compassion because they were fainted and scattered abroad as sheep having no shepherd. He said, "The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest" (*Matthew 9:37-38* KJV). You are a labourer in His harvest. Lift up your eyes and look on the fields.

Lesson: The fields are white unto harvest; you must lift up your eyes and labour for souls.

Action: Lift up your eyes today. See the souls around you who are ready to be harvested, and pray for labourers.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that the harvest is plenteous. Help me to lift up my eyes and see the fields that are white unto harvest.

Say this: I lift up my eyes and look on the fields. The harvest is white already. I am a labourer in God's harvest. I am compassionate toward sinners. I share the hope of eternal life. I am sent to the harvest.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Church Planting
devotionals.memoryVerse: Matthew 16:18 KJV - "And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it."
devotionals.devotional:
Church planting is the essence for which you carry out the great commission. The church of Jesus Christ is never destined to disappear from the scene. Jesus says, "The gates of hell shall not prevail against it" (*Matthew 16:18* KJV). The true church must continue to exist and play her role to the world. The church's unique role to the world and need of mankind cannot be substituted.

The Christian worker must be concerned and committed to church planting, because each true church is a living cell of the body of Christ. It has within it the power to expand and reproduce itself through committed Christian workers. Planting of churches must continue until Christ returns. You must keep on planting churches because the church is God's agent in the world through which He expresses Himself to the world.

No person, village, town, or nation is ever born Christian. Your principal responsibility as a Christian worker is to be evangelistic, reaching out to men, women, boys, girls, and children in various places with the gospel of Christ. As soon as they truly believe in Christ as Lord and Saviour, such converted persons are baptized and made members of the visible Christian community (*Acts 2:46-47* KJV). Plant churches!

Lesson: Church planting is central to the Great Commission; the church is God's redeeming agent on earth.

Action: Pray for your local church and ask God to show you how you can be involved in planting or strengthening a church.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your church. Help me to be committed to planting and establishing churches.

Say this: I am a church planter. The gates of hell cannot prevail against the church. I am committed to planting churches. The church is God's agent in the world. I am part of the church that cannot be stopped.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Training Others
devotionals.memoryVerse: 2 Timothy 2:2 KJV - "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."
devotionals.devotional:
The Lord Jesus Christ sets a great example for you in training other Christian workers. When He started His ministry, He called twelve ordinary men whom He trained for the work of the ministry. He taught them, cared for them, encouraged them, and showed them how to live a life of faith. After His death and resurrection, He commanded them to go and make disciples of all nations (*Matthew 28:19* KJV).

As a trained Christian worker, you must follow this example of our Lord Jesus Christ. It is not enough for you to do the work of the ministry alone; you must train others to do it too. This is what is called multiplication. Paul told Timothy, "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also" (*2 Timothy 2:2* KJV).

There are so many believers in your churches today who are willing to serve God, but they have not been trained. They are like raw materials waiting to be processed. The Christian worker must identify such people and invest his or her life in them. You must take time to disciple, mentor, and train other Christian workers. This is the only way you can reach the world with the gospel of Christ.

Lesson: You must train other Christian workers to multiply the work of the ministry.

Action: Identify someone today who is willing to serve but needs training. Begin to invest in them.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the example of Jesus in training workers. Help me to train and mentor others.

Say this: I train other Christian workers. I identify raw materials and invest my life in them. I multiply the work of the ministry. I am a mentor and a coach. I follow the example of Jesus.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And Peace Of Mind
devotionals.memoryVerse: Philippians 4:6 KJV - "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."
devotionals.devotional:
Today is World Mental Health Day. The world is full of anxiety, stress, and mental turmoil. But as a Christian worker, you are called to live in the peace of God. Scripture says, "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus" (*Philippians 4:6-7* KJV).

This peace is not the absence of trouble; it is an inner peace, a serenity and tranquility that is a legacy from the Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus said, "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (*John 16:33* KJV). You are designed to enjoy Christ's peace in a troubled world. The degree of worry and peace in your heart—which is greater?

You are to cast all your cares upon Him because He cares for you (*1 Peter 5:7* KJV). When you are anxious, you are not trusting God. When you pray with thanksgiving, the peace of God guards your heart and mind. This is your inheritance as a child of God.

Lesson: The Christian worker enjoys the peace of God that passes all understanding by casting all cares upon Him.

Action: Identify one worry you have been carrying. Cast it upon the Lord in prayer and thank Him for the answer.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your peace that passes all understanding. Help me to cast all my cares upon You.

Say this: I am careful for nothing. I pray with thanksgiving, and the peace of God guards my heart and mind. I have peace in a troubled world. I am not anxious. I cast all my cares upon the Lord, for He cares for me.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And The Joy Of The Lord
devotionals.memoryVerse: John 15:11 KJV - "These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full."
devotionals.devotional:
Joy never comes as a result of what is happening outside, nor does it depend on circumstances around you. Joy is the natural outcome of the love of God in you. The heart filled with the love of God is always filled with joy in the Holy Ghost. The Lord says, "These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full" (*John 15:11* KJV).

Christians are designed to live a joyful life daily in all situations before your family members, Christian brethren, and friends. Scripture says, "The joy of the Lord is your strength" (*Nehemiah 8:10* KJV). Your joy is not dependent on your circumstances; it is dependent on your relationship with Christ.

As a Christian worker, you are to measure your spiritual progress by your joy. Can people access you as a joyful Christian worker? Are you living a joyful Christian life? If the joy of the Lord is your strength, then you are strong even in the midst of trials.

Lesson: The joy of the Lord is your strength; it is not dependent on circumstances but on your relationship with Christ.

Action: Choose to rejoice today, regardless of your circumstances. Let the joy of the Lord be your strength.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the joy of the Lord. Help me to live a joyful life in all situations.

Say this: The joy of the Lord is my strength. My joy does not depend on circumstances. My joy is full in Christ. I am a joyful Christian worker. I rejoice in all situations.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 5:18 KJV - "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you."
devotionals.devotional:
Today is Thanksgiving Day in Canada. As a Christian worker, you are called to live a life of gratitude. Scripture says, "In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you" (*1 Thessalonians 5:18* KJV). This is not just a suggestion; it is the will of God for your life.

Gratitude is a choice. It is not based on your circumstances; it is based on your trust in God. Scripture says, "Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name" (*Psalm 100:4* KJV). You are to thank God for who He is, what He has done, what He is doing, and what He will do.

A grateful heart is a powerful weapon against discouragement and depression. When you focus on the goodness of God, your perspective changes. You are to be thankful in all things—both good and difficult. This is the discipline of the mature Christian worker.

Lesson: Gratitude is the will of God; you must give thanks in all circumstances.

Action: List five things you are grateful for today and thank God specifically for each one.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your goodness. Help me to live a life of gratitude in all circumstances.

Say this: In everything, I give thanks. This is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning me. I enter His gates with thanksgiving. I am thankful for who He is and what He has done. I am a grateful Christian worker.

devotionals.topic: The Christian Worker And God's Stewardship Of Resources
devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Peter 4:10 KJV - "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God."
devotionals.devotional:
As a Christian worker, you are a steward of God's resources. This includes your finances, your time, your talents, and the manifold grace of God. Scripture says, "As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God" (*1 Peter 4:10* KJV).

You are to manage God's resources wisely. Scripture says, "Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it" (*Malachi 3:10* KJV). You are to honour God with your finances and trust Him for His provision.

God's resources are not just for you; they are for the work of the kingdom. You are to use what God has given you to bless others. This is the heart of stewardship. When you manage God's resources well, you become a channel of blessing to your generation.

Lesson: You are a steward of God's resources; you must manage them wisely to bless others.

Action: Review your finances and resources today. Ask God to show you how to use them for His kingdom.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for entrusting me with Your resources. Help me to be a faithful steward of all that You have given me.

Say this: I am a steward of God's manifold grace. I manage His resources wisely. I honour God with my finances. I bless others with what He has given me. I am a channel of blessing.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 11:6 KJV - "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him."
devotionals.devotional:
Without faith, it is impossible to please God. As a Christian worker, your ministry is built on faith. Scripture says, "But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" (*Hebrews 11:6* KJV).

Faith is not just believing in God; it is trusting His Word and acting on it. Scripture says, "Faith which worketh by love" (*Galatians 5:6* KJV). Your faith is energized by the love of God that is shed abroad in your heart. When you walk in love, your faith works effectively.

You are to step out in faith, take risks, and trust God for the impossible. Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (*Hebrews 11:1* KJV). You must believe that God is who He says He is and that He will do what He has promised.

Lesson: Faith is essential for the Christian worker; without faith, you cannot please God.

Action: Identify one area where you need to step out in faith today. Trust God and act on His Word.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the gift of faith. Help me to believe You and act on Your Word.

Say this: I have faith in God. I believe He is and that He rewards those who diligently seek Him. My faith works by love. I step out in faith. I trust God for the impossible. I am a believer, not a doubter.

devotionals.memoryVerse: 1 Thessalonians 4:3 KJV - "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication."
devotionals.devotional:
Purity is essential for the Christian worker. Scripture says, "For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication" (*1 Thessalonians 4:3* KJV). You are called to live a pure and holy life, both in your body and in your thoughts.

Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. You are not to defile it with impurity, evil thoughts, evil desires, or deeds. You are required to honour and please God with your body and life. Scripture says, "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (*Matthew 5:8* KJV).

Purity is not just about avoiding sin; it is about being set apart for God's use. You are to live a life that reflects the holiness of God. When you are pure, you are able to see God and walk in His presence.

Lesson: Purity is the will of God; you are called to live a holy and set-apart life.

Action: Examine your heart and mind today. Confess any impurity and ask God to purify you.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can be pure. Help me to live a holy and set-apart life for Your glory.

Say this: I am sanctified. I abstain from impurity. My body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. I am pure in heart and I see God. I honour and please God with my body and life.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Proverbs 11:3 KJV - "The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them."
devotionals.devotional:
Integrity is one of the highest virtues of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "The integrity of the upright shall guide them" (*Proverbs 11:3* KJV). Integrity means that you are consistent in your words and actions. What you say is what you do. You are honest and transparent.

As a Christian worker, you are to be transparent in your dealing with people. Scripture says, "Providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men" (*2 Corinthians 8:21* KJV). Your integrity should be visible to both God and men. You are to be trustworthy, dependable, and reliable.

Without integrity, your ministry will not last. People will not trust you, and God will not bless you. You are to be a person of your word, one who does not waver or compromise on the truth.

Lesson: Integrity guides the upright; you must be honest, transparent, and dependable.

Action: Evaluate your integrity today. Are there any areas where you have not been honest or consistent? Make it right.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You that I can walk in integrity. Help me to be honest and transparent in all my dealings.

Say this: The integrity of the upright guides me. I am honest in the sight of God and men. I am trustworthy and dependable. My word is my bond. I do not compromise on the truth.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Mark 10:45 KJV - "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many."
devotionals.devotional:
You are called to serve, not to be served. Scripture says, "For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many" (*Mark 10:45* KJV). This is the example of Christ. He came to serve, and you are to follow in His steps.

Service is the hallmark of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "For, brethren, ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another" (*Galatians 5:13* KJV). You are to serve others with humility and love. Your service should not be for recognition or reward; it should be a demonstration of the love of Christ.

Service is the key to greatness in the Kingdom. Jesus said, "Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister" (*Matthew 20:26* KJV). You are to be a servant to all, just as Christ served you.

Lesson: You are called to serve others with humility and love, following the example of Christ.

Action: Look for one opportunity to serve someone today without expecting anything in return.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the example of Christ. Help me to serve others with humility and love.

Say this: I am called to serve, not to be served. I follow the example of Christ. I serve others with love. I am great in the Kingdom because I am a servant. I minister to others as Christ ministered to me.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Colossians 3:12 KJV - "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering."
devotionals.devotional:
Compassion is at the heart of the Christian worker. Scripture says, "Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering" (*Colossians 3:12* KJV). You are to be filled with tender mercies and compassion toward others.

Jesus saw the multitudes and was moved with compassion because they were fainted and scattered abroad as sheep having no shepherd (*Matthew 9:36* KJV). Compassion is not just feeling sorry for someone; it is doing something to help them. Compassion moves you to action.

As a Christian worker, you are to be compassionate toward the lost, the hurting, the brokenhearted, and the weak. You are to look for opportunities to show mercy and kindness. This is the love of God in demonstration.

Lesson: Compassion moves you to action; you must put on mercies, kindness, and tenderness toward others.

Action: Today, show compassion to someone who is hurting. Speak a kind word or offer practical help.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for Your compassion toward me. Help me to be compassionate toward others.

Say this: I put on bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, and longsuffering. I am moved with compassion. I help the hurting. I am a tenderhearted Christian worker.

devotionals.memoryVerse: Hebrews 12:1 KJV - "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us."
devotionals.devotional:
Perseverance is essential for the Christian worker. Scripture says, "Let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us" (*Hebrews 12:1* KJV). You are in a race, and you must run with patience and endurance.

The Christian life is not a sprint; it is a marathon. You will face challenges, obstacles, and temptations. But you must not give up. Scripture says, "And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not" (*Galatians 6:9* KJV). Your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

Perseverance is what keeps you going when the going gets tough. It is the determination to finish well. You are to keep your eyes on Jesus, the Author and Finisher of your faith (*Hebrews 12:2* KJV). Do not give up. The prize is at the end of the race.

Lesson: Perseverance keeps you running the race; you must not give up, for your reward is coming.

Action: Identify one area where you are tempted to give up. Determine today to keep running with patience.
devotionals.prayerConfession:
Father, I thank You for the strength to persevere. Help me to run the race with patience and endurance.

Say this: I run with patience the race set before me. I lay aside every weight and the sin that besets me. I am not weary in well doing. In due season, I shall reap. I finish well. I keep my eyes on Jesus.
